transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, what brings me in is... I've been having this issue with eating at night. 

Once I start eating, it's like I completely lose control. It feels like I can almost see myself doing it, and in my head, I'm telling myself to just stop, but my hands just keep going back for more food. I just can't seem to stop myself once it starts.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to prevent weight gain?
No, I don't do that. I've never made myself throw up. I just... I just eat until I'm uncomfortably full, and then I feel terrible about it, but I don't try to get sick afterwards.
Do these eating episodes happen after you have already gone to bed and fallen asleep, or do they happen in the evening before you go to sleep?

It's... well, it's before I go to sleep. I haven't gone to bed yet when it happens. I'm usually just up in the evening, maybe watching TV or trying to wind down from work, and that's when it starts. I don't wake up out of a dead sleep to eat, if that's what you mean.
On average, how many times a week do these eating episodes occur?

I'd say... for the last several months, most weeks have at least one night where I eat like that. Maybe two. 

And then I usually spend the whole next day trying to make up for what I did. I'll skip meals entirely, or set really strict rules for myself about what I'm allowed to eat that day... or I'll go take an extra-long walk just to try and burn it off. But yeah, it's at least once a week lately.
How much does your body shape or weight influence how you judge yourself as a person?

It influences me a lot, honestly. I mean... it didn't always be this way. I used to judge my day by whether I solved a tough design problem at work, or if I helped out down at the theater. But lately, I just look at my stomach in the mirror, and it feels like the whole measure of who I am comes down to whether I look controlled or if I look sloppy.
